title: Cornua cervi degelatinatum inhibits breast cancer stem-like cell properties and metastasis via miR-148a-3p-mediated TGF-beta/Smad2 pathway.
authors: Ma, Yanmiao; Song, Bo; Peng, Jiehao; Wei, Fuxia; Hao, Yuanhui; Wen, Ya; Lv, Huiling; Shi, Xiaoli; Wang, Yonghui; Peng, Tao
one_liner_zh: 研究鹿角胶提取物通过miR-148a-3p调控TGF-beta/Smad2通路抑制乳腺癌干性，仅含分子对接预测小分子与Smad2结合，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Cornua cervi degelatinatum (CCD) is formed by removing the gelatinous substance from deer antlers according to traditional methods. It was first recorded in the Shennong's Classic of Materia Medica and has been included in the Pharmacopoeia of the People's Republic of China. It is commonly used in clinical practice for the treatment of diseases such as cancer and infertility. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aims to investigate the impact of CCD aqueous extract on the proliferation and stemness of breast cancer (BC) cells, with an emphasis on its regulation of miR-148a-3p expression and associated molecular pathways. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Breast cancer cells were treated with various concentrations of CCD to assess its effects on cancer stem cell (CSC) features, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) markers, and overall plasticity. The UALCAN platform was utilized to analyze the relationship between miR-148a-3p and Smad2 expression. Functional experiments involving miR-148a-3p overexpression were performed to elucidate CCD's modulatory effects on the TGF-beta/Smad2 pathway. Furthermore, molecular docking analysis was conducted to predict the binding affinity of CCD's active components to Smad2. RESULTS: The CCD aqueous extract significantly reduced BC cell viability in vitro and dose-dependently suppressed the expression of stemness- and EMT-related proteins. Bioinformatics analysis and luciferase reporter assays validated miR-148a-3p as a direct regulator of Smad2, inhibiting the TGF-beta/Smad2 signaling pathway. Molecular docking revealed strong binding interactions between CCD's active components and Smad2. CONCLUSIONS: CCD exhibits anti-BC effects by working synergistically with miR-148a-3p to inhibit the TGF-beta/Smad2 pathway, thereby reducing BC stemness and EMT progression. These findings provide valuable insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying CCD's therapeutic potential in BC treatment.
abstract_zh: 民族药理学相关性：鹿角胶（Cornua cervi degelatinatum, CCD）是通过传统方法去除鹿角中的胶质物质而形成的。它最早记载于《神农本草经》，并已被纳入《中华人民共和国药典》。临床上常用于治疗癌症和不育症等疾病。研究目的：本研究旨在探讨CCD水提物对乳腺癌（breast cancer, BC）细胞增殖和干性的影响，重点研究其对miR-148a-3p表达及相关分子通路的调控作用。材料与方法：用不同浓度的CCD处理乳腺癌细胞，以评估其对癌症干细胞（cancer stem cell, CSC）特征、上皮-间质转化（epithelial-mesenchymal transition, EMT）标志物及整体可塑性的影响。利用UALCAN平台分析miR-148a-3p与Smad2表达之间的关系。通过miR-148a-3p过表达的功能实验，阐明CCD对TGF-beta/Smad2通路的调节作用。此外，进行分子对接分析以预测CCD活性成分与Smad2的结合亲和力。结果：CCD水提物在体外显著降低BC细胞活力，并剂量依赖性地抑制干性和EMT相关蛋白的表达。生物信息学分析和荧光素酶报告基因实验验证了miR-148a-3p是Smad2的直接调控因子，抑制TGF-beta/Smad2信号通路。分子对接显示CCD活性成分与Smad2之间存在强结合相互作用。结论：CCD通过与miR-148a-3p协同作用抑制TGF-beta/Smad2通路，从而减少BC干性和EMT进展，发挥抗BC效应。这些发现为CCD在BC治疗中治疗潜力的分子机制提供了有价值的见解。
